note: Hand-authored grouping. NOT derived from collection data - taxonomy fields are empty on all 127. Built from binomials resolved through WoRMS to accepted names first, because ~57% of the catalogue names are superseded. Order of groups, and order within each group, is deliberate and load-bearing: do not re-sort. 1884.137.110 was recovered manually: its `collection` field is empty so the collection query never returned it, though it is in Shaw et al. 2017. Harvest on maker_name, not collection. slug is hand-authored and stable: a title edit must never change a URL. representative is the blackest photograph in each group, chosen mechanically by scripts/representatives.mjs so every tile is an object on black rather than a mount board. 1884.137.92 is excluded by rule.

groups.title: Jellyfish, large and small
groups.panelSeed: One body plan — a pulsing bell of almost pure water trailing stinging threads — shown here from a dinner-plate Rhizostoma down to hydromedusae the size of a fingernail, and three times over as the same animal male, female and infant.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 90% of frame below luminance 32, subject   8%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: The man o' war and other floating colonies
groups.panelSeed: A Portuguese man o' war is not one animal but hundreds fused into a single drifting colony — some members stinging, some digesting, some reproducing — and not one of them could survive on its own.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 91% of frame below luminance 32, subject   6%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: Comb jellies and sea butterflies — the see-through swimmers
groups.panelSeed: In open water there is nowhere to hide, so these unrelated animals arrived at the same two answers — become invisible, and swim by beating something — and glass was the only material that could ever show it.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 93% of frame below luminance 32, subject   5%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: Sea squirts and salps
groups.panelSeed: They look like nothing much — a jelly sack pumping water in one opening and out the other — but every one begins life as a swimming tadpole with a stiff rod down its back, which makes these blobs the closest relatives we have anywhere in this collection.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 88% of frame below luminance 32, subject   8%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: Squid, cuttlefish and the paper nautilus
groups.panelSeed: The molluscs that gave up the shell and became hunters — arms, suckers and an eye nearly as good as yours — including an argonaut modelled twice, because the female builds a paper cradle for her eggs and the male is barely a centimetre long.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 81% of frame below luminance 32, subject  13%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: Sea slugs
groups.panelSeed: Take away a snail's shell and it needs another defence, so these fourteen answered with poison, with warning colour, with borrowed stinging cells, and in two cases by stealing working chloroplasts from their food and running partly on sunlight.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 93% of frame below luminance 32, subject   5%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: Sea anemones
groups.panelSeed: An anemone is a stomach on a foot with a ring of poisoned tentacles on top, and these nineteen show how far one simple idea can be pushed — and why the Blaschkas came back to it more often than to anything else in the collection.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 83% of frame below luminance 32, subject  13%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: Corals, sea fans and hydroids — animals that grow like plants
groups.panelSeed: Every branch, fan and stony twig here is a city of tiny anemone-like animals sharing one skeleton — which is why they grow like plants without being plants, and why a coral can be red, blue, feathered or turned to stone.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 95% of frame below luminance 32, subject   3%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: Sea cucumbers, feather stars and brittle stars
groups.panelSeed: A sausage, a feather and a star: look for five-fold symmetry and hundreds of tiny water-powered tube feet, and these eight turn out to be built to the same plan as a starfish — of which this collection, oddly, contains not one.
groups.representativeRationale: blackest ground in the group ( 91% of frame below luminance 32, subject   6%); chosen by scripts/representatives.mjs, not by eye

groups.title: Worms of the seabed
groups.panelSeed: 'Worm' is not a family but a solution, arrived at separately by four different branches of the animal kingdom — including three here that hide the body in a tube and put out a crown so fine it was long mistaken for a flower.

groups.title: Never went to sea
groups.panelSeed: Ten of these 127 never saw salt water — garden slugs, a Roman snail cut open to show its insides, a pond leech — because the Blaschkas supplied classrooms as well as museums, and a lecture room needed the animal in the cabbage patch as much as the one in the Bay of Naples.
